model: the GNS baseline of the paper (6.6M parameters, trained on the same training simulations), forward prediction
look: the renderer, lights and camera of the PhysX and NeuWorld tiles of the same item

launcher_tower.note: The ball knocks four blocks out of the two lowest layers; the upper layers drop onto the remaining blocks and stay stacked, whereas in PhysX the whole tower comes down.
launcher_tower.label: GNS
launcher_tower.sub: graph network simulator; input: scene graph and action
launcher_tower.position_error_source: mean distance of the moving objects from the PhysX states over the whole simulation (6 s), as for the NeuWorld tile

pendulum_jenga.note: The pendulum knocks two of the three top-layer blocks to the floor and the third stays on the tower, whereas in PhysX all three fall.
pendulum_jenga.label: GNS
pendulum_jenga.sub: graph network simulator; input: scene graph and action
pendulum_jenga.position_error_source: mean distance of the moving objects from the PhysX states over the whole simulation (6 s), as for the NeuWorld tile
